name: Medi Assist Healthcare Services Ltd
title: Medi Assist Healthcare Services Ltd - 544088 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Medi Assist Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 3.9% YoY to INR241.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.4%; group retention held at about 90.5% in H1.
summary.overview: Management said Paramount integration is complete, with all group corporates and claims now on the MAtrix platform, and Q2 is the first like-to-like quarter post-acquisition. Q2 operating revenue grew 3.9% YoY to INR241.5 crore, while H1 operating revenue grew 13.0% to INR478 crore, with the gap driven by lost Paramount retention and revenue recognition on a 1/365 basis. EBITDA margin expanded 331 bps YoY in Q2 to 20.4%, and reported PAT for H1 rose 60.2% to INR49.2 crore. The board approved a share buyback of up to INR49.3 crore at INR425 per share, and the company announced a policy of returning about 50% of cumulative adjusted free cash flow over rolling five-year periods.

financial_highlights.change: +60.2% YoY; underlying INR46.1 crore vs INR30.7 crore, excluding one-time derivative gain classified as exceptional last quarter
vs INR852.4 crore at FY26 end
vs INR260.5 crore at FY26 end; zero debt

segments.name: India TPA
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR437.5 crore (+11.9% YoY), 91.5% of operating revenue; Q2 revenue INR219.6 crore (+1.2% YoY). Government H1 revenue INR57.3 crore (+14%); retail H1 revenue INR45.5 crore (-1.8%).

segments.name: Group (within TPA)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR334.7 crore (+13.7% YoY), about 70% of revenue; group premiums managed grew 21.8% YoY, market share 34.1%; retention about 90.5% in H1.

segments.name: Platform and HBA
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR19.8 crore (+69.8% YoY), 4.2% of operating revenue; Q2 revenue INR11.2 crore (+94.8% YoY), 4.6% of Q2 revenue. Platform premiums managed INR9,648 crore (+24.8%).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: H1 revenue INR20.7 crore (+1.1% YoY), 4.3% of operating revenue; Q2 revenue INR10.7 crore (+7.7% YoY). Claims processed from 141 countries across 21,000 providers in H1.

guidance_outlook: No specific revenue guidance given; management said TPA will grow at par or faster than the market on premium share.
Retention expected to return to 93-94% in three to four quarters from Q2 FY27 as Paramount integration settles.
Same-store growth on retained group business expected to continue in the 8-9% range, with a possible rise to 9-10% from GST input tax credit benefits for corporates.
Revenue lag of 2-3 quarters versus premium growth; revenue trend expected to normalise over the next three to four quarters.
Steady-state core business EBITDA margin said to be 22-23%; current 20.4% absorbs investments in tech and international.

Capital allocation: about 50% of cumulative adjusted FCF returned over rolling five years via dividends (ordinary or special) and buybacks; first step is buyback of up to INR49.3 crore at INR425 per share, funded from internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Paramount integration complete: 100% of corporates served by Medi Assist and 100% of claims running on MAtrix; headcount about 800 lower than at acquisition.
Platform processed over 7 million claims in H1 FY27 and handles over 1 million claims a month.
Four insurers contracted for retail platform (about INR758 crore incremental premiums) went live in Q2; platform live in Southeast Asia for international business.
Bundles (fraud, intelligent adjudication, network as a service) decoupled from MAtrix, allowing insurers to use them on their own core systems; one such signup so far.
demand_pricing: Retention of about 90.5% in H1, marginally up QoQ; management attributes drop to churn in Paramount tail-end corporates and the December cyber incident at Paramount affecting Jan-April renewals.
About 80% of retention losses replaced by new business; contract liability rose to INR321.7 crore from INR280.2 crore at FY26 end.
Group premiums industry growth about 15.8% in H1 per GI Council; Medi Assist grew over 21%. Management says it is growing faster than market.
Blended TPA fee of about 2.7% on group and retail; management views this as good value for insurers amid EOM rationalisation.
Per-claim revenue for value-add bundles could be 5-10 times the base platform SaaS revenue (INR100-120 per claim cited), but these are not yet in reported revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How has industry premium growth compared with Medi Assist's like-to-like growth, and how will it reach low double-digit organic growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Group premiums industry grew about 15.8% in H1 versus Medi Assist over 21% including acquisitions; same-store growth expected at 8-9%, rising to 9-10% with GST ITC benefits; retention to recover to 93-94% in 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q2 TPA revenue growing only 1-3% and what is the outlook for H2 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is booked on a 1/365 basis so lost Q1 accounts continue in revenue for a year; management gave no formal guidance but said contract liability rose INR40-50 crore since March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retention fall, and what steps will restore it?
qa_highlights.answer: Churn in Paramount tail-end corporates and a cyber incident delayed renewals by about a quarter; full integration, 800+ fewer staff and continuous innovation are expected to restore 93-94% retention in 3-4 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EOM consultation paper's impact and is there an outsourcing opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TPA fees are transparent and grossed up in premiums; insurers may outsource servicing and claims control, where Medi Assist's platform and AI could help. No early pricing signals were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20.4% margin sustainable, and what levers remain?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin absorbs overlapping international and platform costs; management still targets steady-state 22-23% in core business, with revenues from new platform implementations yet to kick in.

qa_highlights.question: Why is group revenue growing 4% when premiums managed grew about 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to revenue lag on 1/365 basis, installment premium recognition, and lost April renewals; no revenue guidance, but group expected to grow at par or faster than market.

risks_watch: Group retention at 90.5% versus historical 93-94%; recovery timing of 3-4 quarters is key to watch.
Revenue lag of 2-3 quarters means Q2 optics (operating revenue +3.9%) may persist into H2.
Pending IRDAI EOM consultation paper could pressure TPA economics; no pricing signal yet.
Platform/tech revenue largely base SaaS; value-add bundle revenue yet to appear in reported numbers.
International revenue growth slowed to 1.1% in H1 while overlapping costs persist.
summary.management_tone: Confident on integration completion, cash generation and margin recovery, but cautious and non-committal on near-term revenue and retention, declining to give formal guidance and attributing weakness to timing and churn.
key_quotes: Q2 is our first like -to-like quarter since the Paramount acquisition, w ith integration now complete and all Paramount claims running on MAtrix.
The accounting revenue translation will typically lag by 2 to 3 quarters, and you should see that in the numb ers going forward.
we still sort of stand by that our steady -state margins are 22%, 23% in the core business, and that continues to be a focus area to get, back there at the earliest.

adds.what: Four insurers on retail platform (about INR758 crore incremental premiums) went live in Q2; platform live in Southeast Asia for international business

growth.why: Management guides same-store growth of 8-9% (possibly 9-10%) and TPA growth at or above market, backed by group premiums up 21.8% and market share of 34.1%, though retention (~90.5% vs 93-94% historic) and a 2-3 quarter revenue lag weigh on near-term revenue; no specific revenue guidance was given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 20.4% (+331 bps YoY) with management still targeting steady-state core margin of 22-23%, though current levels absorb tech and international investments.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Platform has gone live for four retail insurers (about INR758 crore incremental premiums) and Southeast Asia, but no new physical capacity or capex was guided; handles over 1 million claims a month.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Group premiums managed grew 21.8% in H1 with 34.1% market share, and same-store growth is guided at 8-9% (possibly 9-10%), though retention at 90.5% versus 93-94% historically and a 2-3 quarter revenue lag weigh on near-term revenue.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed; the company is asset-light SaaS and the capital focus is on a INR49.3 crore buyback rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Same-store growth could rise to 9-10% from GST input tax credit benefits for corporates, but management gave no formal revenue guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 operating revenue grew only 3.9% YoY and TPA revenue just 1.2%, with a 2-3 quarter lag and retention at 90.5%, so near-term revenue optics could disappoint even though management avoided formal guidance.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Value-add bundles (fraud, intelligent adjudication, network as a service) are decoupled from MAtrix and could be worth 5-10 times base SaaS per claim (INR100-120 cited), but only one insurer has signed so far and none is in reported revenue.

rows.label: Buyback of up to INR49.3 crore at INR425 per share
rows.why: Board has approved the buyback funded from internal accruals, with the company holding INR268.3 crore cash and zero debt.

rows.label: Retention recovery to 93-94%
rows.why: Management expects retention to return from about 90.5% in H1 to 93-94% as Paramount integration settles, and contract liability already rose to INR321.7 crore from INR280.2 crore.

rows.label: IRDAI EOM consultation paper
rows.why: The pending paper could pressure TPA economics, but no pricing signal has been given and management says the fee is transparent (blended around 2.7%).

tone.note: Management was confident on Paramount integration, cash generation and margin recovery, but cautious on near-term revenue and retention, avoiding formal guidance; analysts pressed on why group revenue grew about 4% while premiums managed grew about 12%, and on the 1/365 revenue lag and EOM regulator
